limits.description: One original 1647 English witness was read; no collation with Lilly's printer's copy or upstream authorities, nor 1659 correction.
Aphorism9 says no urine OR consent, with uncertain Boolean scope; do not silently normalize to absent both.
Aphorism14 uses 'or' and 'if two ... be so affected'; exact quantified antecedent and else branch remain ambiguous.
Aphorism15 has the printed 'it's doubtfull ... will dye' phrase and alternative ruler scope; no categorical death rule established.
Aphorism18's above-Earth house enumeration omits the tenth while claiming the rest under; do not fill or repair missing house without another witness.
Aphorism19 literally reads 'great fear of recovery' despite surrounding mortality claims; preserve polarity.
Aphorism27 lord-of-one / dispositor-of-other and affliction conditions retain local syntactic ambiguity.
Aphorism28 contains alternative Body, Spirits and Animals statements, including contrary clause; not modern mental illness.
Aphorism29 enumerates house sets but leaves houses not named; do not infer their illness disclosure status.
Aphorism33 references an infortune 'both times' with natal/decumbiture ambiguity; benefic beams at one of the times except the adverse prognosis.
Aphorism34 combines natal, sickness and Revolution ascendants with an unclear referent of 'same'; do not invent a solar-return definition.
Aphorism43 says judge Saturn contrary to Mars conditions, but does not fully enumerate logical negations.
No historical claimed outcome is independently verified; no patient chart or dated physician visit appears within admitted aphorisms.
Planetary hour, orientation, station, combustion, lunar illumination, and aspects must not be conflated; no orb, rate or calendar-day conversion is specified for these maxims.
The urine/consent procedure reflects 17th-century practice and grants no modern consent or medical authority.
Aphorism40 imputes delay to patient misgovernment/carelessness, an unsupported attribution about actual patient behaviour.
Several illness and death assertions have categorical source rhetoric; no clinical validity, probabilistic calibration, treatment efficacy or predictive transfer is established.

Original errata page PDF888 has four printed entries in admitted pages: p284 line14 read if; line37 delete semicolon; p285 line4 read her; line11 read therein. The exact body-line targets and applicability are not all resolved; retain them as an independent witness rather than silently applying.
Aphorism4 movable quick ending/common variation and aphorism30 movable variation/common recurrence are different source claims; do not harmonize them.
Aphorism8 urine was sometimes of essence may mean formerly or occasionally; no external lexical source collated.
Aphorism12 lights they after Sun or Moon permits either-vs-both reading, unlike explicit both in aphorism11.
Aphorism20 though under Earth may refer to ascendant lord, Moon or aspect; no uniquely resolved target.
Aphorism23 if unfortunate may qualify only death or both prolongation and death; printed errata284/14 read if may bear on benevolent clause.
Aphorism34 exact opposite natal ascendant implies natal seventh but the source conjunctive house list also includes four others.
Aphorism43 Mars masculine/oriental/above-Earth list could be conjunctive or separate aggravations; source not unambiguous.
Aphorisms8–9 both address urine-without-consent under differing assignments; original or and where no consent is remain unresolved.
